Bill number: HB1163
<bill_text>
SENATE BILL 1019
 By White

 HOUSE BILL 1163

 By Stevens

 AN ACT to amend Chapter __ of the Public Acts of 2025
 (1st Ex. Sess. – SB 6001 / HB 6004); and
 Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 49, Chapter 13
 and Title 49, Chapter 3, relative to education
 funding for public charter schools.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE STATE OF TENNESSEE:

 SECTION 1. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-3-103(d)(3), is amended by

adding the language "or public charter school" after the language "Explain how an LEA".

 SECTION 2. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-3-105, is amended by deleting

subsection (d) and substituting instead the following:

 (d)

 (1) The funding that a student generates pursuant to this section must be

 administered and allocated by the department to the LEA in which the student is

 a member for the duration of the student's membership in the LEA, except that:

 (A) The funding a student generates pursuant to subdivision

 (c)(3) must not be allocated to the LEA, but must be maintained by the

 department; and

 (B) The state share of the funding a public charter school student

 generates for an LEA pursuant to this section must not be allocated to the

 LEA, but must be allocated directly to the public charter school.

 (2) A student's membership in an LEA begins on the first day of the

 student's membership and ends on the last day of the student's membership in

 the LEA, except that the membership of a student who graduates early is

 extended to the student's expected graduation date for funding purposes.

 SECTION 3. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-3-316, is amended by adding the

language "or public charter school" after the language "LEA" wherever it appears in subsection

(c) and by adding the following as a new subsection:

 (f)

 (1) The commissioner, in consultation with the comptroller of the

 treasury, shall develop, revise as necessary, and prescribe a standardized

 system of financial accounting and reporting for all public charter schools,

 including appropriate forms or other documentation. This system must be

 designed to facilitate year-to-year and agency-to-agency comparison, as well as

 adequately indicating the sources and uses of all funds received by each public

 charter school. The commissioner shall review the fiscal public school records in

 all public charter schools to the end that the expenditure of funds, whether for

 current operation and maintenance purposes, capital outlay purposes, and other

 school purposes, are properly accounted for and safeguarded.

 (2) The commissioner may require public charter schools that receive

 allocations of state education funding pursuant to part 1 of this chapter or

 otherwise to comply with one (1) or more of the requirements established for

 LEAs in this section, as the commissioner deems appropriate or applicable.

 SECTION 4. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-13-112, is amended by deleting

subsection (a) and substituting instead the following:

 (a)

 (1) A local board of education shall allocate to the public charter school

 an amount equal to:

 (A) The local student-generated funds for member students in the

 public charter school for the prior year in alignment with the TISA

 pursuant to chapter 3, part 1 of this title;

 (B) The average per pupil state and local funds received by the

 district in the current school year above those required by the TISA for

 each member student in the public charter school in the prior year;

 (C) The per student state and local funds received by the LEA for

 member students in the public charter school in the current school year

 beyond the prior year's membership; and

 (D) All appropriate allocations under federal law or regulation,

 including, but not limited to, IDEA and ESEA funds.

 (2) The department of education shall allocate directly to the public

charter school an amount equal to the state student-generated funds for member

students in the public charter school for the prior year in alignment with the TISA

pursuant to chapter 3, part 1 of this title.

 (3) Federal funds received by the LEA must be disbursed to public

charter schools authorized by the LEA by either joint agreement on shared

services by individual public charter schools or sub-grants to a public charter

school for the public charter school's equitable share of the federal grant based

on eligible students. The allocation must be made in accordance with the

policies and procedures developed by the department of education.

 (4) Each LEA shall include as part of its budget submitted pursuant to §

49-2-203, the per pupil amount of local money it will pass through to public

charter schools during the upcoming school year, including all calculations listed

in this section. Allocations to public charter schools during that year must be

 based on the calculated amounts. The LEA shall distribute the portion of local

 funds it expects to receive in no fewer than nine (9) equal installments to public

 charter schools in the same manner as state funds are distributed pursuant to

 chapter 3 of this title. An LEA shall adjust local payments to public charter

 schools, at a minimum, in October, February, and June, based on changes in

 revenue, student membership, or student services. All funds received by a public

 charter school must be spent according to the budget submitted or as otherwise

 revised by the public charter school governing body, subject to the requirements

 of state and federal law.

 SECTION 5. Sections 1 and 3 of this act take effect upon becoming a law, the public

welfare requiring it. For rulemaking purposes, Sections 2 and 4 of this act take effect upon

becoming a law, the public welfare requiring it. For all other purposes, Sections 2 and 4 of this

act take effect July 1, 2025, the public welfare requiring it.
</bill_text>

<summary>
The bill would change how Tennessee funds public charter schools. The state would send a charter school the state share of funding generated by its students, rather than sending that share to the local education agency (LEA). Other student-generated funding would go to the LEA while the student is a member, except for funding under a cited provision that the department would retain. For funding purposes, a student who graduates early would remain a member until the student’s expected graduation date.

A local board of education would allocate to a charter school local student-generated funds based on the school’s prior-year members, current-year state and local funds above TISA requirements based on those members, and funds for current-year members beyond the prior-year count. It would also allocate appropriate federal funds. The education department would send the charter school state student-generated funds based on prior-year members. An LEA would provide federal funds to charter schools it authorizes through agreed shared services or sub-grants based on eligible students, under department procedures.

Each LEA would include its calculated per-student local payment to charter schools in its upcoming budget and use that amount for allocations. It would pay expected local funds in at least nine equal installments and adjust payments at least in October, February, and June for changes in revenue, membership, or student services. Charter schools would spend funds under their governing bodies’ budgets, as revised, and applicable law.

The bill would add charter schools to wording in Sections 49-3-103(d)(3) and 49-3-316(c). It would also require the education commissioner, in consultation with the comptroller, to establish a standardized charter-school financial accounting and reporting system and review charter-school fiscal records. The commissioner could apply other listed LEA requirements to charter schools that receive state education funding. These accounting and wording changes would take effect upon enactment. The funding changes would take effect upon enactment for rulemaking and July 1, 2025, for other purposes.
</summary>

assessments.summary_quote: The bill would add charter schools to wording in Sections 49-3-103(d)(3) and 49-3-316(c).
assessments.rationale: Identifies the amended provision and conveys its extension to public charter schools.

assessments.summary_quote: The state would send a charter school the state share of funding generated by its students, rather than sending that share to the local education agency (LEA). Other student-generated funding would go to the LEA while the student is a member, except for funding under a cited provision that the department would retain.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the general allocation rule and direct charter-school payment, but does not identify subdivision (c)(3) as the funding the department must retain.

assessments.summary_quote: Other student-generated funding would go to the LEA while the student is a member, except for funding under a cited provision that the department would retain. For funding purposes, a student who graduates early would remain a member until the student’s expected graduation date.
assessments.rationale: Conveys funding throughout actual membership and the extension through an early graduate's expected graduation date.

assessments.summary_quote: The bill would add charter schools to wording in Sections 49-3-103(d)(3) and 49-3-316(c).
assessments.rationale: Identifies subsection 49-3-316(c) and conveys its extension to charter schools.

assessments.summary_quote: It would also require the education commissioner, in consultation with the comptroller, to establish a standardized charter-school financial accounting and reporting system
assessments.rationale: Includes the responsible officials and standardized system, but omits necessary revisions, forms or documentation, comparative design requirements, and accounting for all sources and uses of funds.

assessments.summary_quote: It would also require the education commissioner, in consultation with the comptroller, to establish a standardized charter-school financial accounting and reporting system and review charter-school fiscal records.
assessments.rationale: Conveys mandatory fiscal-record review but omits its required purpose of ensuring expenditures across school purposes are properly accounted for and safeguarded.

assessments.summary_quote: The commissioner could apply other listed LEA requirements to charter schools that receive state education funding.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the commissioner's discretion to apply the referenced LEA requirements to state-funded charter schools.

assessments.summary_quote: A local board of education would allocate to a charter school local student-generated funds based on the school’s prior-year members
assessments.rationale: Conveys the local board's allocation of local student-generated funding using prior-year charter membership.

assessments.summary_quote: A local board of education would allocate to a charter school local student-generated funds based on the school’s prior-year members, current-year state and local funds above TISA requirements based on those members
assessments.rationale: Captures the funding sources and relevant years but omits the district-average per-pupil calculation.

assessments.summary_quote: A local board of education would allocate to a charter school local student-generated funds based on the school’s prior-year members, current-year state and local funds above TISA requirements based on those members, and funds for current-year members beyond the prior-year count.
assessments.rationale: Conveys funding for membership growth but does not specify that this allocation equals the per-student state and local funds received by the LEA.

assessments.summary_quote: It would also allocate appropriate federal funds.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the local board's obligation to allocate appropriate federal funding; the named federal programs are illustrative.

assessments.summary_quote: The education department would send the charter school state student-generated funds based on prior-year members.
assessments.rationale: Conveys direct department allocation of state student-generated funding based on prior-year charter membership.

assessments.summary_quote: An LEA would provide federal funds to charter schools it authorizes through agreed shared services or sub-grants based on eligible students, under department procedures.
assessments.rationale: Includes the authorized-school limitation, distribution methods, and department procedures, but omits the requirement that sub-grants represent the school's equitable share of the federal grant.

assessments.summary_quote: Each LEA would include its calculated per-student local payment to charter schools in its upcoming budget and use that amount for allocations.
assessments.rationale: Conveys budget disclosure of the per-pupil amount and its use for allocations, but omits the obligation to include all required calculations in the budget.

assessments.summary_quote: It would pay expected local funds in at least nine equal installments
assessments.rationale: Conveys the minimum number and equality of installments, but omits distribution in the same manner as state funds.

assessments.summary_quote: It would pay expected local funds in at least nine equal installments and adjust payments at least in October, February, and June for changes in revenue, membership, or student services.
assessments.rationale: Includes the mandatory adjustment months and all three grounds for adjustment.

assessments.summary_quote: Charter schools would spend funds under their governing bodies’ budgets, as revised, and applicable law.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the budget restriction, governing-body revisions, and applicable legal requirements.

assessments.summary_quote: These accounting and wording changes would take effect upon enactment. The funding changes would take effect upon enactment for rulemaking and July 1, 2025, for other purposes.
assessments.rationale: Accurately distinguishes immediate effectiveness for Sections 1 and 3 from the rulemaking and general effective dates for Sections 2 and 4.
